locator.section: Eq. 8.2, arrow 3.1, inductive (secondary: C4H9+ -> C2H5+ + C2H4)

evidence.curator_note: adduct corrected to null (convention G): the species undergoing this reaction is an EVEN-ELECTRON cation (charge +1, radical_electrons 0) - a fragment/secondary-fragmentation precursor - NOT the [M]+. radical molecular ion. precursor_mz corrected to the m/z of the ion that actually undergoes the drawn reaction (convention G: the reacting species sets adduct + precursor_mz); it previously carried the neutral molecule's molecular-ion m/z, which describes the parent EI experiment rather than this step's precursor (sibling record IMS8-EQ8.1c already used the reacting-ion convention). (was 100.0883, now 57.0693 = n_butyl_cation.) Secondary fragmentation of the m/z-57 n-butyl cation: inductive cleavage of the C2-C3 bond expels ethylene and gives the ethyl cation C2H5+ (m/z 29, 20%). Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs: Eq. 8.2 is a thermochemical fragmentation map (log k printed above each reaction arrow, heats of formation printed below each species), not a curved-arrow figure. All electron moves here are curator-inferred from the mechanism-type label printed under the reaction arrow; none is drawn on the page. ONE double-barbed arrow: the C2-C3 sigma pair becomes the new C3=C4 pi bond of ethylene, moving the charge from C4 onto C2 (the ethyl cation).

Cross-linked to IMS_8_2_ind_3_1. Correct cleavage (their C5-C8 = my C2-C3) and charge migration to the ethyl cation (their C5+ = my C2+), but the ethylene fragment is written '[C]8[C]11' with a SINGLE C-C bond (each carbon divalent) instead of the C=C double bond; this record uses genuine ethylene C3=C4. Bond-order under-specification only.
